markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if all relevant elections are completed and certified.
markets.rules_primary: If at least 16 members of the House Republicans lose re-election in 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Members count as losing re-election if they actively seek re-election (by filing candidacy or appearing on ballot) but fail to win. This includes losses in primaries, general elections, runoffs, retention elections, or recalls. Members who retire, withdraw before primaries, die, resign, or are disqualified do not count as losses. If redistricting forces two group members against each other, the loser counts. Members who switch parties after issuance remain part of the original group. If a member loses their party primary but wins as an independent, they did not lose re-election.

Losses in 2026 House primaries and runoffs held before this market opened count, including for members who later leave office. Members who ran for a different office, such as the Senate, are not counted. Party is as listed by the Clerk of the House when this market opened. Non-voting delegates and the Resident Commissioner are not counted.

According to FIDE regulations, when players have equal Elo ratings on the FIDE Top Women Players Standard Rating List, the tiebreaking methodology is as follows:
Number of rated games played - The player who has played more rated games in the rating period is ranked higher
Date of birth - If the number of games is also equal, the younger player (later birth date) is ranked higher
Alphabetical order by surname - If both criteria above are still tied, players are ordered alphabetically by their family name

markets.rules_primary: If OpenAI has a model on the Pareto frontier of Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index vs. Cost per Intelligence Index Task chart on Dec 31, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: Resolves at 10:00 AM ET on Dec 31, 2026, using the chart on artificialanalysis.ai with the Pareto line shown. A model counts for the creator Artificial Analysis lists for it. A model is on the frontier if the chart's Pareto line passes through it: no other plotted model has an Intelligence Index at least as high and a Cost per Task at least as low, both unrounded, with one of the two strictly better; models with identical values are both on it. A model without a positive Cost per Task is not plotted and cannot be on the frontier.

markets.early_close_condition: If an event described in the Payout Criterion occurs, expiration will be moved to an earlier date and time in accordance with Rule 7.2.
markets.rules_primary: If the cumulative sum of Heating Degree Days (HDD) at Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (station identifier KCVG, WMO identifier 72421) is below 1,250.00 between Oct 1, 2026 and Dec 31, 2026, the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The official observing station is Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (station identifier KCVG, WMO identifier 72421). The specified local timezone is America/New_York. The accumulation period includes Oct 1, 2026 through Dec 31, 2026.

A Heating Degree Day (HDD) value measures how far a day's average temperature falls below 65°F. For each local calendar day, HDD equals 65 minus the daily average temperature in Fahrenheit, floored at zero. Days averaging 65°F or warmer contribute zero HDD; the excess above 65°F is not counted and does not offset colder days. For example, a day averaging 40°F contributes 25.00 HDD, and a day averaging 72°F contributes 0.00 HDD, not -7.00. The daily value is the HDD (65) figure published by The Weather Company for the station; if that figure is not published, it is calculated from The Weather Company's "Hourly Mean(F)" value, which is the arithmetic mean of the hourly temperatures reported for that day. The cumulative sum is the total of these daily values across every day in the specified time period.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if certified election results are published.
markets.rules_primary: If the margin of victory for Shen Bo-yang in the 2026 Taipei mayoral election is at or above 2%, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The margin of victory is the vote share received by Shen Bo-yang minus the vote share received by the candidate that finishes immediately behind Shen Bo-yang if Shen Bo-yang wins, or the candidate that finishes first if Shen Bo-yang loses. If Shen Bo-yang wins, the margin will be positive; if Shen Bo-yang loses, the margin will be negative; if Shen Bo-yang ties for first place, the margin shall be 0.

Each margin range is inclusive of its lower bound and exclusive of its upper bound, and no rounding shall be applied. For example, for consecutive ranges of 5-6% and 6-7%, a margin of 5.99999% resolves within the 5-6% range, while a margin of exactly 6% resolves within the 6-7% range. If Shen Bo-yang runs under multiple parties or is listed multiple times, votes attributable to the same underlying candidate will be summed.
markets.title: Will the margin of victory for Shen Bo-yang in the 2026 Taipei mayoral election be at least 2%?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the economic data is released.
markets.rules_primary: If the MoM percent change in The Conference Board Leading Economic Index for the U.S. for November 2026 is above -0.4%, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The Leading Economic Index refers to The Conference Board Leading Economic Index® (“LEI”) for the United States. This market will resolve using the month-over-month percent change for November 2026 stated in the first Conference Board release that reports the November 2026 LEI.

The market will use the percent change expressly reported by The Conference Board and will not independently calculate the change from index levels. Subsequent revisions will not affect settlement.

This market does not refer to the LEI index level, its six-month change or diffusion index, the Coincident Economic Index, or the Lagging Economic Index.

markets.rules_secondary:
Unblocking means any federal court, including the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit or the U.S. Supreme Court, lifting, staying, narrowing or reversing the vacatur in Catholic Legal Immigration Network, Inc. v. Rubio, No. 1:26-cv-00858 (S.D.N.Y.), so that the visa suspension policy may resume operation.

An administrative or temporary stay that permits the policy to resume counts, even if it is later dissolved
A ruling that narrows the vacatur to the named plaintiffs counts, because the policy may then resume as to everyone else
Denial of a stay motion, or no ruling permitting the policy to resume, resolves this market NO
If the Executive Branch rescinds the vacated policy and issues a new suspension under different authority, that does NOT count, because it is not an action of the federal judiciary
markets.title: Will federal courts unblocked the policy suspending immigrant visa processing for 75 countries before Nov 24, 2026?

U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit

events.title: US 10Y Treasury yield at 10:15am ET · US new-home sales

markets.rules_primary: If the value of the S&P 500 index, as calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, on December 23, 2026 at 10:14:59 AM EST is at least 6800.00, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Observation: Uses the closing index level of the one-minute candle ending Dec 23, 2026 at 10:15am EST: the S&P 500 value as of 10:14:59 AM EST on December 23, 2026, the preceding minute's final second. Each market compares that same observation with its stated fixed index-point strike. At least includes equality, which resolves Yes. The named economic event provides context; a delayed or rescheduled release does not automatically move the observation time.

Source Agencies (in priority order): S&P Dow Jones Indices, Pyth Network (official S&P 500 feeds), Bloomberg, WSJ, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, CNBC. If sources conflict, this order governs; any remaining dispute is resolved by Kalshi under Rule 7.1.

What counts as the S&P 500 value:
Only the index level calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, to two decimal places.
ETFs, futures, options, perpetuals, and constituent stock prices do not count.
If no time of day is specified, the official closing value for each trading day is used. Intraday, open, high/low, and pre-/after-hours values do not count.

Trading days:
Only days with an official S&P 500 close count (Eastern Time). Weekends and market holidays are ignored.
If the specified observation is at or after an early close or a halt ending trading for the day, the official close designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices governs.

Index changes:
Changes to constituents, weightings, divisor, or methodology do not affect the contract.
If the index is renamed, rebranded, or re-coded but its record continues, the contract stays open. If it is discontinued with no successor, the No-data rule applies.

No data:
If no Source Agency publishes a value by the Expiration Date (including if markets are closed for the entire period), all markets resolve No, unless a "No data" strike is listed, in which case that strike resolves Yes.

Corrections:
Corrections published before Expiration govern; corrections published after Expiration are ignored.
If Kalshi finds a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published. If none is published by the Expiration Date, the No-data rule applies.
